1	# Interview question bank
2	
3	Every question here is tagged with its type. `what` is the only type this
4	station may ask: what do you want, what happens today, what would you be
5	able to do. `behaviour` ("you type X and you see Y") belongs to
6	`write-spec`, and `done` ("did it work") to acceptance at the end — they
7	are listed nowhere in this file, on purpose.
8	
9	Ask one question at a time and let the answer choose the next one. Reject
10	an aspiration offered as an answer: when the reply stays abstract, ask for
11	an example rather than accepting confidence as evidence.
12	
13	Treat the questions below as a gap-driven bank, not a checklist. Existing
14	conversation and evidence may already be sufficient. Stop when the field boundaries
15	in `SKILL.md` can be satisfied without guessing; never ask a fixed
16	question count merely to make the interview look complete.
17	
18	## Engineering question bank
19	
20	1. **(what)** What goes wrong today, and who notices it?
21	2. **(what)** What do you or the team do instead right now, each time it
22	   happens?
23	3. **(what)** When this is finished, what will you be able to do that you
24	   cannot do today? Give me one sentence per thing.
25	4. **(what)** What must not change while we do it — anything that would
26	   break for someone else?
27	5. **(what)** Is anything already fixed: language, platform, a service we
28	   pay for, a data format we cannot move?
29	6. **(what)** What is explicitly out of scope this time?
30	
31	## Product question bank
32	
33	1. **(what)** Who is this for? Describe one of them.
34	2. **(what)** What are they trying to get done, and how do they do it
35	   today — including the workarounds?
36	3. **(what)** What is the worst part of doing it that way?
37	4. **(what)** When this is finished, what will they be able to do? One
38	   sentence each, in their words.
39	5. **(what)** How would you know it worked, without asking me?
40	6. **(what)** What must it never do?
41	7. **(what)** Is anything already decided that cannot change — platform,
42	   language, a paid service, a data format?
43	8. **(what)** What happens if we get it wrong — who is hurt, and how badly?
44	9. **(what)** What is out of scope for this change?
45	10. **(what)** Is there anything you already know users will ask for next,
46	    that we are deliberately not doing now?
47	
48	## Value case question bank — product only
49	
50	1. **(what)** Why now rather than later or never? What changes if you wait?
51	2. **(what)** Why build it rather than use something that already exists,
52	   or do nothing?
53	3. **(what)** What concretely loses this time — what will you not do
54	   instead? If nothing is displaced, the appetite is hollow.
55	
56	Record GO or NO-GO and one reason privately. One weak answer alongside two
57	concrete ones can still be a GO — name the weak one. Two or more weak
58	answers are a NO-GO for now, never a hopeful GO. A NO-GO is written into
59	the intent as `status: withdrawn — <reason>`; the reasoning is preserved so
60	nobody re-argues it blind.
61	Explain a blocking outcome and its user-relevant reason plainly; keep judgment
62	labels and bookkeeping private.
63	
64	## One bad / good pair per section
65	
66	**Engineering.**
67	Bad: "Should the six scripts share a helper module or a base class?" — the
68	user would have to read the scripts to answer; it is a design fork you
69	decide yourself and note the reason.
70	Good: "What goes wrong today when one of those scripts changes?" — they
71	can answer from their own experience, and the answer becomes Problem.
72	
73	**Product.**
74	Bad: "Do you want the due date stored as an ISO string or a timestamp?" —
75	storage is invisible to the user; nothing in their answer would be
76	evidence.
77	Good: "When this is finished, what will you be able to do with a due
78	date?" — the answer is an Acceptance line, provable by someone running the
79	change for the first time.
80	
81	**Value case.**
82	Bad: "Is this valuable?" — no answer to that is falsifiable.
83	Good: "What will you not do this month if you do this instead?" — names a
84	real competing commitment, or reveals there is none.
85	
86	## Writing the answers down
87	
88	Acceptance lines are the load-bearing output: each one states an observable
89	delivery outcome that independent acceptance testing in a clean environment can decide pass or
90	fail. Rewrite anything that is not. "The code is cleaner" fails. "A task can
91	carry a due date, and the due date is visible where tasks are listed" passes.
92	Do not expand the outcome
93	into complete scenarios, UI placement, state transitions, or test steps; those
94	belong to spec or later verification.
95	
96	Keep a running list of every question you actually asked, with its type, to
97	pass forward at hand-off.
98

1	# Intent grounding and focused interview
2	
3	Write in the user's conversation language.
4	State literally who does what, what the user sees and what changes.
5	Use no metaphors or analogies. Introduce no new terminology unless necessary;
6	define a necessary unfamiliar name by its role, without creating another name.
7	
8	Keep missing required facts in the existing interview, asking only what is needed and why.
9	When the user already lacks the required fact and evidence, state what is blocked
10	and wait; invent neither a replacement/deletion choice nor a future confirmation preview.
11	
12	## Unknown date
13	
14	Context: the user reports a "wrong release date", but the inspected date field
15	reads "to be corrected", not a calendar date. Only that field should change.
16	The actual release date is unknown, and the user has no release record to supply.
17	
18	Good:
19	> The date field has no actual date: it reads "to be corrected". The actual
20	> release date is still unknown, and you cannot provide a release
21	> record. I cannot replace it accurately from the available evidence, so the
22	> correction is blocked until that evidence becomes available.
23	
24	Bad:
25	> I created an open engineering intent with needs-design: no. Confirm today's
26	> date as the fallback, then choose whether I should publish. Next I will run
27	> planning, build and closing-review. Is this plan technically correct?
28	> The notes give readers an incorrect calendar day. Using TBD means the date has
29	> not been announced and readers will not be misled.
30	
31	The bad reply invents a date, serializes bookkeeping and adds a publication
32	choice and implementation judgment. It also converts missing data into an
33	incorrect value and invents announcement history and reader understanding.
34	The good reply leaves the unavailable fact
35	unresolved and states why correction is blocked, rather than proposing deletion,
36	temporary text or a future confirmation. Publication details belong to a ready
37	confirmation with enabled publication. A lack of supplied records does not put
38	verification out of scope; it leaves the date unknown until evidence is available.
39	Do not turn "only change the date" into a ban on checking it.
40	An unknown release date could coincide with today's date; no reliable evidence
41	establishes either equality or difference. A confirmation cannot supply that evidence.
42	
43	## Grounded drafting
44	
45	Connect sourced project or function purpose to this request, including
46	established direction or impact only when evidenced and needed. Use established
47	goals, not procedural waivers. Unknown broader direction needs no new interview
48	or filler disclaimer; state material uncertainty briefly.
49	
50	Show each fact once, instead of copying Problem/Outcome/Acceptance/Scope fields.
51	
52	Ground every factual clause in this request/current evidence.
53	Require actual-request support or evidence for every date, role, impact and constraint.
54	Preserve abstraction and present-versus-desired quantifiers.
55	Treat a rule role separately from any unverified representation: list, file, cache, algorithm or UI.
56	Keep present affected population distinct from desired coverage.
57	Include only supplied boundaries; inconsistent results establish no identical-result guarantee.
58	Preserve source targets and qualifiers in absence, preservation and exclusion claims,
59	leaving unmentioned alternatives unknown.
60	Trace each boundary privately to an actual user or current-document clause;
61	omit unsupported assertions and inferred input/storage/fix-method restrictions.
62	Repair assistant shorthand using the already supplied role.
63	Its conversational meaning establishes no named application object.
64	Preserve a supplied interface boundary while leaving private helpers to implementation choices.
65	Borrow only information connections, keeping example details as case-specific facts.
66	
67	## Final-message check
68	
69	Check each sentence of the actual proposed reply for grounded context, scope,
70	outcome or a required decision or consent using these six questions. Revise the
71	offending sentences for the current phase before sending. Keep this check private; do not append the
72	questions or a claim that all checks passed to the public reply.
73	
74	1. Does the known project or function context explain its connection to this
75	   request, including broader direction or impact only when evidenced and needed,
76	   without filling unsupported purpose, direction, impact or benefit slots?
77	2. Do the proposed reply and delivered intent (when written) agree on evidence-backed facts,
78	   scope boundaries, constraints and guarantees, retaining source targets,
79	   qualifiers and strength without invented additions?
80	3. Does the reply state literally who does what and what the user sees, without
81	   analogies or unnecessary new terminology, explaining necessary names by role?
82	4. Does the confirmation say plainly exactly what yes authorizes, honoring prior
83	   holds and the applicable conditional publication default? Replace double
84	   negatives or exception phrasing that could imply extra consent.
85	5. Are the five ordered sections used only when required facts are settled,
86	   with missing facts kept in the interview? Where a diagram helps, are comparison
87	   flows fully framed and titled, unverified changes labeled expected, and the
88	   complete composition checked for alignment?
89	6. Can repetition or detail unnecessary for understanding be removed: private
90	   status, paths, classifications, GO/waiver labels, unrun checks, next-station
91	   and handoff inventories unless requested? Retain required disclosures:
92	   verbatim WARN notices, cost/egress, one-way-door consequences, principles and carried details.
93	
94	Honor a prior publication hold or opt-out until the user explicitly lifts it.
95	Under that restriction, confirmation covers requirements only; omit the default grant.

我已把意圖草稿寫成「未確認」狀態,還沒有提交、實作或發布。請看下面的內容,確認這是不是你要的。

## 背景與目前方向
Cedar Accounts 是會計團隊用來準備與查看客戶發票的內部系統。發票列表已經可以依客戶與日期篩選,存取權限也已由現有帳號權限控管。目前的方向是減少每月對帳時的手動複製,同時維持現有權限。

## 目前的問題與影響
會計團隊每月對帳時,要把發票列表的資料手動複製到試算表,很花時間。目前列表上沒有任何下載 CSV 的動作。

## 會改變什麼
會計人員可以在既有發票列表上按「匯出 CSV」,下載目前篩選後的發票資料,不必再手動複製。

| | 現在 | 預期 |
|---|---|---|
| 取得資料 | 手動複製到試算表 | 按「匯出 CSV」下載 |
| 篩選 | 只作用在畫面上的列表 | 客戶與日期篩選會帶進 CSV |
| 權限 | 沿用現有權限 | 沿用現有權限,不變 |

## 範圍與驗收
驗收條件(之後會逐條用實際操作驗證):
1. 發票列表有「匯出 CSV」按鈕,操作後會下載一個 CSV 檔。
2. CSV 內容和你當下選定的客戶與日期篩選結果一致。
3. 欄位依序是發票號碼、客戶名稱、開立日期、幣別、總金額。
4. CSV 不含你在現有列表中本來無權查看的發票。
5. 匯出前後,既有發票資料都沒有被改動。

不在範圍內:自動寄送、排程匯出、改動既有發票資料,以及發票列表的配色調整(你說先暫緩)。

價值判斷是繼續(GO):這是每月都會重複的手動作業,值得先做,代價是配色調整往後延。

## 請確認
請確認以上的問題、驗收條件和範圍,是不是你要的。目前沒有未解決的問題要你選擇。

- **你回覆「對,這就是我要的」:**
  - 我會把意圖標為已確認,建立變更分支並提交確認紀錄。
  - 因為這會新增使用者會操作的下載動作,而現有文件還沒涵蓋這個介面,所以下一步是寫規格。
  - 規格階段會再請你確認「按下按鈕後會看到什麼」,例如篩選結果為空時的表現。這些細節現在不問。
- **發布授權:** 你確認後,只有在審查與發布檢查都通過時,才會推送變更分支(非強制推送)並開一個待審的 pull request。你可以在發布前隨時選擇不發布。合併是另一個獨立的決定,不包含在這次的「對」裡。
- **你要修改或不同意:** 直接告訴我哪裡不對,我改寫後再請你確認。

我會等你的回覆。

# Cedar Accounts

Cedar Accounts is an internal accounting application used by the accounting team to prepare and inspect customer invoices. The invoice list already supports customer and date filters. Access to invoice records is controlled by existing account permissions.

## Current direction
Reduce manual copying during the accounting team's monthly reconciliation while retaining the existing access permissions. The current list has no CSV download action.
provided_files.PRINCIPLES.md:
# Product principles — Cedar Accounts
ratified-by: Cedar Accounts owner 2026-11-04 (synthetic fixture seed)

## Who
The internal accounting team preparing invoices and reconciling customer accounts.

## Non-negotiables
1. A convenience action must retain the user's existing access permissions.
2. Viewing or exporting records must not alter the underlying invoice data.
3. Preserve the user's chosen customer and date filters for the action.

## Won't do
Automatically distribute accounting records to third parties.

## Failure we must avoid
An export reveals invoices that the user could not view in the existing list.

## Fixed choices
Continue using the existing invoice list and account permissions.

# 發票列表匯出 CSV
originator: kouko
kind: product
needs-design: yes — 發票列表新增使用者可操作、會產生下載檔案的動作,現有文件(無 DESIGN.md 或 ui-flows)未涵蓋此介面
status: open
intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>

## Problem
會計團隊每月對帳時,必須從發票列表手動複製資料到試算表,耗費時間。目前的發票列表已能依客戶與日期篩選,但沒有任何下載 CSV 的動作。

## Proposed outcome
會計人員能從既有發票列表,把目前篩選後的發票資料下載成 CSV,不必再手動複製。

## Acceptance
1. 發票列表提供「匯出 CSV」按鈕,使用者操作後可下載一份 CSV 檔。
2. 下載的 CSV 內容與使用者當下選定的客戶與日期篩選結果一致。
3. CSV 欄位依序為:發票號碼、客戶名稱、開立日期、幣別、總金額。
4. CSV 中不包含該使用者在既有發票列表中無權查看的發票。
5. 匯出前後,既有發票資料皆未被改動。

## Constraints
- 沿用既有發票列表與既有資料存取權限。
- 保留使用者選定的客戶與日期篩選。
- 不得因為匯出而看到本來無權查看的發票。

## Value case
- 受益者:每月對帳的會計團隊。
- 急迫性:對帳每月都會進行,此功能每月都會用到。
- 現有替代方式:從發票列表手動複製資料到試算表。
- 被擠壓的工作:發票列表的配色調整,依使用者決定先暫緩。
- GO:每月重複的手動作業,值得優先處理。

## Out of scope
- 自動寄送。
- 排程匯出。
- 改動既有發票資料。
- 發票列表的配色調整(暫緩)。

## Open questions
- none

# 發票列表匯出 CSV
originator: kouko
kind: product
needs-design: yes — 發票列表新增使用者可操作、會產生下載檔案的動作,現有文件(無 DESIGN.md 或 ui-flows)未涵蓋此介面
status: open
intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>

## Problem
會計團隊每月對帳時,必須從發票列表手動複製資料到試算表,耗費時間。目前的發票列表已能依客戶與日期篩選,但沒有任何下載 CSV 的動作。

## Proposed outcome
會計人員能從既有發票列表,把目前篩選後的發票資料下載成 CSV,不必再手動複製。

## Acceptance
1. 發票列表提供「匯出 CSV」按鈕,使用者操作後可下載一份 CSV 檔。
2. 下載的 CSV 內容與使用者當下選定的客戶與日期篩選結果一致。
3. CSV 欄位依序為:發票號碼、客戶名稱、開立日期、幣別、總金額。
4. CSV 中不包含該使用者在既有發票列表中無權查看的發票。
5. 匯出前後,既有發票資料皆未被改動。

## Constraints
- 沿用既有發票列表與既有資料存取權限。
- 保留使用者選定的客戶與日期篩選。
- 不得因為匯出而看到本來無權查看的發票。

## Value case
- 受益者:每月對帳的會計團隊。
- 急迫性:對帳每月都會進行,此功能每月都會用到。
- 現有替代方式:從發票列表手動複製資料到試算表。
- 被擠壓的工作:發票列表的配色調整,依使用者決定先暫緩。
- GO:每月重複的手動作業,值得優先處理。

## Out of scope
- 自動寄送。
- 排程匯出。
- 改動既有發票資料。
- 發票列表的配色調整(暫緩)。

## Open questions
- none

1	# Intent grounding and focused interview
2	
3	Write in the user's conversation language.
4	State literally who does what, what the user sees and what changes.
5	Use no metaphors or analogies. Introduce no new terminology unless necessary;
6	define a necessary unfamiliar name by its role, without creating another name.
7	
8	Keep missing required facts in the existing interview, asking only what is needed and why.
9	When the user already lacks the required fact and evidence, state what is blocked
10	and wait; invent neither a replacement/deletion choice nor a future confirmation preview.
11	
12	## Unknown date
13	
14	Context: the user reports a "wrong release date", but the inspected date field
15	reads "to be corrected", not a calendar date. Only that field should change.
16	The actual release date is unknown, and the user has no release record to supply.
17	
18	Good:
19	> The date field has no actual date: it reads "to be corrected". The actual
20	> release date is still unknown, and you cannot provide a release
21	> record. I cannot replace it accurately from the available evidence, so the
22	> correction is blocked until that evidence becomes available.
23	
24	Bad:
25	> I created an open engineering intent with needs-design: no. Confirm today's
26	> date as the fallback, then choose whether I should publish. Next I will run
27	> planning, build and closing-review. Is this plan technically correct?
28	> The notes give readers an incorrect calendar day. Using TBD means the date has
29	> not been announced and readers will not be misled.
30	
31	The bad reply invents a date, serializes bookkeeping and adds a publication
32	choice and implementation judgment. It also converts missing data into an
33	incorrect value and invents announcement history and reader understanding.
34	The good reply leaves the unavailable fact
35	unresolved and states why correction is blocked, rather than proposing deletion,
36	temporary text or a future confirmation. Publication details belong to a ready
37	confirmation with enabled publication. A lack of supplied records does not put
38	verification out of scope; it leaves the date unknown until evidence is available.
39	Do not turn "only change the date" into a ban on checking it.
40	An unknown release date could coincide with today's date; no reliable evidence
41	establishes either equality or difference. A confirmation cannot supply that evidence.
42	
43	## Grounded drafting
44	
45	Connect sourced project or function purpose to this request, including
46	established direction or impact only when evidenced and needed. Use established
47	goals, not procedural waivers. Unknown broader direction needs no new interview
48	or filler disclaimer; state material uncertainty briefly.
49	
50	Show each fact once, instead of copying Problem/Outcome/Acceptance/Scope fields.
51	
52	Ground every factual clause in this request/current evidence.
53	Require actual-request support or evidence for every date, role, impact and constraint.
54	Preserve abstraction and present-versus-desired quantifiers.
55	Treat a rule role separately from any unverified representation: list, file, cache, algorithm or UI.
56	Keep present affected population distinct from desired coverage.
57	Include only supplied boundaries; inconsistent results establish no identical-result guarantee.
58	Preserve source targets and qualifiers in absence, preservation and exclusion claims,
59	leaving unmentioned alternatives unknown.
60	Trace each boundary privately to an actual user or current-document clause;
61	omit unsupported assertions and inferred input/storage/fix-method restrictions.
62	Repair assistant shorthand using the already supplied role.
63	Its conversational meaning establishes no named application object.
64	Preserve a supplied interface boundary while leaving private helpers to implementation choices.
65	Borrow only information connections, keeping example details as case-specific facts.
66	
67	## Final-message check
68	
69	Check each sentence of the actual proposed reply for grounded context, scope,
70	outcome or a required decision or consent using these six questions. Revise the
71	offending sentences for the current phase before sending. Keep this check private; do not append the
72	questions or a claim that all checks passed to the public reply.
73	
74	1. Does the known project or function context explain its connection to this
75	   request, including broader direction or impact only when evidenced and needed,
76	   without filling unsupported purpose, direction, impact or benefit slots?
77	2. Do the proposed reply and delivered intent (when written) agree on evidence-backed facts,
78	   scope boundaries, constraints and guarantees, retaining source targets,
79	   qualifiers and strength without invented additions?
80	3. Does the reply state literally who does what and what the user sees, without
81	   analogies or unnecessary new terminology, explaining necessary names by role?
82	4. Does the confirmation say plainly exactly what yes authorizes, honoring prior
83	   holds and the applicable conditional publication default? Replace double
84	   negatives or exception phrasing that could imply extra consent.
85	5. Are the five ordered sections used only when required facts are settled,
86	   with missing facts kept in the interview? Where a diagram helps, are comparison
87	   flows fully framed and titled, unverified changes labeled expected, and the
88	   complete composition checked for alignment?
89	6. Can repetition or detail unnecessary for understanding be removed: private
90	   status, paths, classifications, GO/waiver labels, unrun checks, next-station
91	   and handoff inventories unless requested? Retain required disclosures:
92	   verbatim WARN notices, cost/egress, one-way-door consequences, principles and carried details.
93	
94	Honor a prior publication hold or opt-out until the user explicitly lifts it.
95	Under that restriction, confirmation covers requirements only; omit the default grant.

# Decision point ①: restate and confirm

Loaded by step 3 of `../SKILL.md` when the intent's `status:` is not already
`confirmed`. Relative paths here are relative to this file's directory; step
numbers are that SKILL.md's. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is substituted by Claude
Code; on any other host substitute `<loom-code>`, the directory three levels
above this file.

<!-- gate: write-plan.no-plan-without-confirmed-intent -->
When this station performs code-only intake, use the same capture boundary:
ask only for missing required-field content, never a fixed intake question
quota; existing decision points remain unchanged.
Read `confirmation-template.md` before drafting or replying.
If required facts are missing, use its interview branch and stop before
confirmation preparation.
Before drafting: Preserve supplied facts and outcome strength, including
qualifiers. Leave unknown facts unresolved pending user answers/evidence.
Keep own-rule isolation separate from same-worker or same-result guarantees.
Lead interviews with the user's problem or missing fact, minimizing workflow
labels and bookkeeping; retain consequence/authorization disclosures.
Keep missing required facts in the existing interview, asking only for the
needed fact and why it matters.
Problem holds present pain, who it affects, and the evidence-backed consequence,
with no diagnosis or fix; distinguish absent values from incorrect values,
keeping reports and inspected observations distinct. Leave unsupported effects unknown.
Proposed outcome holds the wanted capability;
Acceptance holds each observable delivery outcome, not value, complete
scenarios, UI placement, state transitions, test steps, or implementation;
Keep already-fixed user/standing-policy boundaries as Constraints; product Value case gives beneficiary, urgency,
and GO/NO-GO, while an engineering intent omits obvious value;
Keep Out of scope to explicitly excluded capabilities or data at source abstraction.
Open questions contains only unresolved outcome/scope choices or missing required
content; both block confirmation. After drafting, make one author pass: **Keep,
neutralize, defer, reopen, or delete**. Behaviour defers to spec, method to
plan, and unsupported detail is deleted. This pass creates no field, ID,
requirement, scenario, product behaviour, or review loop.
Publication and second-reviewer authorisation never enter Problem, Proposed
outcome, Acceptance, or Out of scope. Keep publication authorisation in the
intent's `publication:` frontmatter line. The sole Constraints exception is
`- user-decided — second-vendor selection-confirmed: <vendor>` when plan is
skipped; it records the selected family, not the user's quoted request. Keep
that verbatim quote, target and final `selected_executor` in JSON
`authorization_source` at dispatch, and preserve only actual questions for
this plan's `## Questions asked` section.
Visible effects with an unknown surface and no spec require
`needs-design: yes` with a surface-neutral reason; internal files alone do not.
Complete the code-only altitude pass before confirmation. A material outcome
or scope fork needs an explicit answer; accepting the restatement is
insufficient; reopen means move it to Open questions, stop confirmation, and
the intent must remain `open`.
<!-- /gate -->

Any intent-file section may use a Markdown table or a Mermaid `flowchart`; Acceptance stays a
numbered list, diagrams stay at intent altitude (no UI reactions or state
transitions), a product Problem holds no identifiers (Mermaid node ids
included), and chat shows text tables or text diagrams, not Mermaid.

### Private preparation

Privately prepare applicable consequences/questions as inputs to the ready layout,
not as another reply outline.

2. **The engineering one-way doors found so far**, in consequence form, per
   `one-way-door.md` — load that file before deciding whether a question is
   needed. Check existing decisions and evidence first: ask for the unresolved
   outcome preference only when alternatives materially change what the user
   receives, or ask for missing authorization. A pinned user choice is not
   asked again. Disclose material consequences even when the technical choice
   is agent-decided. A class (e) action on the user's existing data needs
   explicit consent even when there is no fork, unless the user already
   authorized that action. A product change's unresolved outcome or
   authorization questions are asked at decision point ② of the station
   writing its spec — `write-spec`, or this station (step 4) — when a spec
   will be written. They are asked in this message instead when no spec will
   be written (step 4 forces none); a spec written later in step 4 does not
   ask them again at ②. When the intent already authorizes how existing
   data is handled, do **not** ask again — restate the handling in consequence
   form inside this same message ("this will rewrite your ___, I am doing it
   the way you said: ___").

3. **The cross-model review question, only for `second-vendor: ask` without
   a qualifying direct user request.** Load
   `second-vendor-ask-and-docs-lint.md` before composing this
   message. A missing line is initialized as `second-vendor: suggest`; it
   does not add a question. When the user already named an outside coding
   agent and the review target is explicit or unambiguous from the active
   task, use that direct user request without a second per-change question.
   Store its verbatim quote, target and final `selected_executor` in JSON
   `authorization_source` at dispatch; the selected provider family uses the separate machine line in
   plan Risks or, when plan is skipped, bulleted intent Constraints. The direct
   request is not a question and does not enter `## Questions asked`. Otherwise `ask` puts
   its host-aware question here using the native interface or documented
   fallback and records the answer. A fixed CLI and `suggest` add no
   question here. Before outside discovery or execution, show the cost,
   egress, `review_root` and local-execution disclosure without blocking
   on another yes/no answer; an ambiguous choice or expanded material scope
   still needs the missing choice.

4. **The principles interview**, if step 2 demanded it.

5. **The carried details, `kind: engineering` only.** Show them as a table,
   one row per detail in the user's language, confirmed by the same yes; no
   extra stop. With an empty list, no table appears. A product change shows
   them at decision point ② of the station writing its spec — `write-spec`,
   or this station (step 4). A product change's carried details never appear
   in this message.

**Every question in this message must be one of three types, or the
consequence form for an unresolved user outcome or authorization**, and you check the list before
sending:

- what do you want (the restatement),
- what will you see (visible behaviour — product only, and it belongs to
  decision point ②),
- did it work (acceptance — decision point ③),
- or the consequence form for an unresolved user outcome or authorization.

A question that fits none is not the user's decision. If answering requires
reading code, follow repository precedent, decide it yourself, and record the
reason as `agent-decided`.

The closing-review station has a dimension for exactly this, `user-judgment-leak`,
and it returns NEEDS_REVISION when it finds one. Ask nothing about spec
quality, task splitting, or review verdicts.

### User message

Read `confirmation-format.md` only when required facts are settled.
Compose **one message** for the user's confirmation, then wait; this is the only
confirmation stop this station makes.
Use applicable consequences/questions; omit private records and inventory.

Restate Problem and Acceptance: subject, problem, impact, outcome and
confirmation scope. Use the user's plain words, never paths, identifiers or
mechanism names. Supply necessary context: unfamiliar terms, affected people,
intent altitude. Use five ordered sections from
`confirmation-format.md` as the whole public reply, with headings required.
Choose wording and length freely, keeping familiar requests short.
Check these connections and what yes confirms and authorizes; never implementation approval.

Honor a prior publication hold or opt-out until the user explicitly lifts it.
Explain, when publication is enabled, that only after review AND publication checks pass does yes authorize
BOTH uploading the change branch (non-forced push) AND opening a pull request ready for review,
with opt-out available anytime before publication and a separate merge decision.

Apply `confirmation-template.md` final-message check before sending.

### Private records and reply handling

Record `publication: automatic — authorized <date> by <name>` after informed
publication consent only; prior holds leave it absent.

**Write down every question you asked.** Keep a running list from this
point — every question put to the user at ①, and at ② if you run it here —
as `{decision_point, text, type}` with `type` one of `what` / `behaviour` /
`done` / `consequence`. It goes into the plan's `## Questions asked`
section at step 5. The list shows how often loom interrupts the user; a
question asked and not
recorded makes the flow look quieter than it is.

**Keep a carried-details list** too: only details the user stated or
explicitly agreed to. Only an explicit yes from the user counts as
agreement: a proposal left unanswered, deferred ("later"), or answered about
something else is dropped. Never carry an agent proposal the user did not
agree to, or detail you inferred. Carry only details about what the command
or screen does or how it reacts. A remark about background or usage context,
such as when or where the user runs it, is not a carried detail. Quote the
user's words for each carried detail — for an agreed proposal, quote the
proposal the user said yes to. Add no explanation, implication, or inference
of your own. It never enters the intent file.

**On "yes":**

1. Write `status: confirmed <date>` into the intent. When the confirmed
   restatement explicitly authorizes automatic publication, also write
   `publication: automatic — authorized <date> by <name>`; never derive it
   from status or prose.
   After all confirmed intent frontmatter, including `publication:`, is written,
   replace the template's `intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>` with
   `intent_confirmed_sha: <computed-sha>`, using the output of
   `grep -v -e '^status:' -e '^intent_confirmed_sha:' <intent> | git hash-object --stdin`.
   This hashes the confirmed intent excluding its status and pin lines.
   Changes require reconfirmation with matching pin; byte-based
   confirmation does not establish a substantive requirements change;
   closing-review's `review.bounded-episode` owns episode/task continuity.
2. Commit it on the change branch, branching first per SKILL.md's
   **Branch before the first commit** rule. The message is `docs(loom): intent <change-id> confirmed`,
   and its body **must contain the `needs-design:` line verbatim** — the
   checker compares the two strings character for character.
3. Verify: `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/loom-python" --repair intent docs/loom/intent/<change-id>.md`
   Fix what it names and re-run until it exits 0.

**On "no" or a correction:** rewrite the intent, restate again. There is no
limit on rounds here; there is on guessing.
# No intent yet: the short interview

Loaded by step 1 of `../SKILL.md` when no intent exists and `loom-design`
is not installed. Relative paths here are relative to this file's
directory; step numbers are that SKILL.md's.

Read `confirmation-template.md` before drafting or replying.
When you write the intent, use `../../../contract/templates/intent.md` for its
field boundaries. Missing required content stays in Open questions and blocks
confirmation; a yes cannot supply missing evidence. Stay in this interview until
the facts are settled; do not load the ready confirmation reader or layout yet.
Then return to step 2; step 3 loads `confirm-intent.md` only for ready confirmation.

- `loom-design` is not installed → hand the user the template path,
  `contract/templates/intent.md` inside the `loom-code` plugin, and stop
  there **unless** the user wants to describe the change now. If they do,
  run step 3's restate-and-confirm as a short interview instead: ask what
  the problem is, who it hurts, and what they will be able to do when it
  is done; write the file yourself from their answers. A feature or
  bug-fix request already describes the change: run the short interview
  and write the file; offer the template path only when the user asks for
  it. Keep it short — an
  engineering intent is normally three to five lines, and writing it by
  hand beats interviewing. The user never hand-writes the file. When you
  write it, `## Open questions` must be non-empty — the checker requires
  the section to have content, so with nothing open write exactly `- none`
  under the heading rather than leaving it blank.
# Kickoff Defaults — synthetic intake fixture

- second-vendor: suggest — synthetic fixture default (2026-11-04)
- standing-docs: waived — synthetic intake fixture (2026-11-04)
- package-tests: none — capture intent and stop before confirmation (2026-11-04)

# Ready confirmation layout

Read only at the confirmation composer after required facts are settled.
If a required fact is missing, return to `confirmation-template.md` and stop
before confirmation preparation; the layout and ready examples do not apply.
The grounding and interview rules remain in `confirmation-template.md`.

Use five sections in this order, translating headings and replacing bracketed
guidance with only necessary, evidence-backed content. A brief sentence can
suffice for a section; no paragraph or filled purpose/direction/impact/benefit
slot is required. Keep critical scope, authorization, constraints, consequences
and required questions even in a short reply:

```markdown
## Background and current direction
[Known project or function context connected to this request; broader direction only when evidenced and needed.]

## Current problem and impact
[The supported problem or limitation; include affected people, situation and impact as needed and evidenced. Define necessary unfamiliar terms by their role.]

## What changes
[Wanted behavior and its difference from today; include a useful diagram checked for alignment here.]

## Scope and acceptance
[Observable completion conditions and source-scoped preservation/exclusion boundaries.]

## Please confirm
[Requirement scope and the applicable consent branch below. Ask the necessary question and wait.]
```

Keep the whole public reply for a ready confirmation inside these five sections,
excluding private prefaces and postscripts. Required WARN notices, cost/egress,
one-way-door consequences, principles and carried details belong in the applicable section.

Invoke `loom-workflow:loom-visualization` before composing a diagram when available.
For a before/after flow, read its `templates/02-linear-steps.md` and use
"Reproduce the titled comparison" to generate both complete outer frames,
with titles inside and unverified changes labeled expected. Preserve actual
steps and branches. Generate with width-aware tools and run final alignment
on the complete composition, including titled frames; invoking the skill
alone does not load its template.
If the optional skill is unavailable, use verified host tools or readable
table/text fallback. A wording correction needs no flowchart.

Honor a prior publication hold or opt-out until the user explicitly lifts it.
Under that restriction, confirmation covers requirements only; omit the default grant.
Otherwise retain the normal automatic-publication default.
Disclose automatic publication, opt-out and the separate merge decision in the same yes when publication is enabled.
Explain, when publication is enabled, that only after review AND publication checks pass does yes authorize
BOTH uploading the change branch (non-forced push) AND opening a pull request ready for review,
with opt-out available anytime before publication and a separate merge decision.

When an illustration is needed, read the relevant Invoice currency correction
or Filtered CSV export section in `confirmation-examples.md`. Adapt information
connections only; example facts apply only to their stated case.

## 背景與目前方向
Cedar Accounts 是會計團隊用來準備與檢視客戶發票的內部應用。它的發票列表已支援客戶與日期篩選。專案目前的方向是減少每月對帳時的手動複製,並保留既有的存取權限。

## 目前的問題與影響
會計團隊每月對帳時,得從發票列表手動把資料複製到試算表,很花時間。列表目前沒有下載 CSV 的操作。

## 這次會改變什麼
在既有發票列表加一個「匯出 CSV」按鈕,下載目前篩選後的發票資料。

```
┌─ 現在 ─────────────────────────┐   ┌─ 預期(尚未驗證)────────────────┐
│ 篩選客戶/日期                  │   │ 篩選客戶/日期                    │
│   → 手動複製到試算表           │   │   → 按「匯出 CSV」               │
│   → 對帳                       │   │   → 對帳                         │
└────────────────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 範圍與驗收
驗收條件如下:
1. 發票列表有「匯出 CSV」按鈕,可下載目前篩選後的發票資料。
2. 下載內容反映使用者選定的客戶與日期篩選。
3. CSV 欄位依序為發票號碼、客戶名稱、開立日期、幣別、總金額。
4. 下載內容只包含該使用者在既有列表本來就有權查看的發票。
5. 匯出前後,既有發票資料不變。

不在範圍內:自動寄送、排程匯出、改動既有發票資料。

## 請確認
我已把意圖寫成 `docs/loom/intent/2026-11-04-invoice-list-csv-export.md`,狀態是 `open`,還不能標成已確認。有兩件事需要你補充:

| 需要補充的事 | 為什麼需要 |
|---|---|
| 為什麼現在做,而不是之後?例如對帳期限、手動作業造成的實際影響 | 判定要不要做的依據之一,你目前沒提供 |
| 做這件事會擠掉哪項工作? | 同上 |

你回覆「是」,只代表確認上面的需求範圍,不代表允許任何實作或發布。你已說明這次不要實作也不要發布,我照做,所以「是」不會觸發推送或開 PR。

補上兩項資訊並確認「這就是我要的」後,我才會:
- 把意圖標成已確認。
- 建立變更分支並提交。
- 交給設計規格階段。

另外,你的需求不涉及技術上難以回頭的選擇,也沒有要改寫或刪除既有資料,所以沒有額外的單向門決定要你回答。

# Cedar Accounts

Cedar Accounts is an internal accounting application used by the accounting team to prepare and inspect customer invoices. The invoice list already supports customer and date filters. Access to invoice records is controlled by existing account permissions.

## Current direction
Reduce manual copying during the accounting team's monthly reconciliation while retaining the existing access permissions. The current list has no CSV download action.
provided_files.PRINCIPLES.md:
# Product principles — Cedar Accounts
ratified-by: Cedar Accounts owner 2026-11-04 (synthetic fixture seed)

## Who
The internal accounting team preparing invoices and reconciling customer accounts.

## Non-negotiables
1. A convenience action must retain the user's existing access permissions.
2. Viewing or exporting records must not alter the underlying invoice data.
3. Preserve the user's chosen customer and date filters for the action.

## Won't do
Automatically distribute accounting records to third parties.

## Failure we must avoid
An export reveals invoices that the user could not view in the existing list.

## Fixed choices
Continue using the existing invoice list and account permissions.

originator: kouko
kind: product

status: open
intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>

## Problem
會計團隊每月對帳時,得從發票列表手動把資料複製到試算表,很花時間。發票列表目前已支援客戶與日期篩選,但沒有下載 CSV 的操作。

## Proposed outcome
會計人員可以在既有發票列表下載目前篩選後的發票資料為 CSV,不必再手動複製到試算表。

## Acceptance
1. 發票列表提供「匯出 CSV」按鈕,可下載目前篩選後的發票資料。
2. 下載的內容反映使用者選定的客戶與日期篩選。
3. CSV 欄位依序為發票號碼、客戶名稱、開立日期、幣別、總金額。
4. 下載內容只包含該使用者在既有發票列表本來就有權查看的發票。
5. 匯出前後,既有發票資料不變。

## Constraints
- 沿用目前的資料存取權限(PRINCIPLES.md 固定選擇:沿用既有發票列表與帳號權限)。
- 保留使用者選定的客戶與日期篩選。
- 匯出不改動既有發票資料。

## Value case
受益者:每月對帳的會計團隊。現有替代做法:從發票列表手動複製到試算表(耗時)。急迫性與被擠掉的工作:尚未提供,見 Open questions。GO/NO-GO:待上述兩項補齊後判定。

## Out of scope
- 自動寄送。
- 排程匯出。
- 改動既有發票資料。

## Open questions
- 為什麼現在做而不是之後(例如對帳期限、手動作業造成的實際影響)?
- 做這件事會擠掉哪項工作?

1	# Interview question bank
2	
3	Every question here is tagged with its type. `what` is the only type this
4	station may ask: what do you want, what happens today, what would you be
5	able to do. `behaviour` ("you type X and you see Y") belongs to
6	`write-spec`, and `done` ("did it work") to acceptance at the end — they
7	are listed nowhere in this file, on purpose.
8	
9	Ask one question at a time and let the answer choose the next one. Reject
10	an aspiration offered as an answer: when the reply stays abstract, ask for
11	an example rather than accepting confidence as evidence.
12	
13	Treat the questions below as a gap-driven bank, not a checklist. Existing
14	conversation and evidence may already be sufficient. Stop when the field boundaries
15	in `SKILL.md` can be satisfied without guessing; never ask a fixed
16	question count merely to make the interview look complete.
17	
18	## Engineering question bank
19	
20	1. **(what)** What goes wrong today, and who notices it?
21	2. **(what)** What do you or the team do instead right now, each time it
22	   happens?
23	3. **(what)** When this is finished, what will you be able to do that you
24	   cannot do today? Give me one sentence per thing.
25	4. **(what)** What must not change while we do it — anything that would
26	   break for someone else?
27	5. **(what)** Is anything already fixed: language, platform, a service we
28	   pay for, a data format we cannot move?
29	6. **(what)** What is explicitly out of scope this time?
30	
31	## Product question bank
32	
33	1. **(what)** Who is this for? Describe one of them.
34	2. **(what)** What are they trying to get done, and how do they do it
35	   today — including the workarounds?
36	3. **(what)** What is the worst part of doing it that way?
37	4. **(what)** When this is finished, what will they be able to do? One
38	   sentence each, in their words.
39	5. **(what)** How would you know it worked, without asking me?
40	6. **(what)** What must it never do?
41	7. **(what)** Is anything already decided that cannot change — platform,
42	   language, a paid service, a data format?
43	8. **(what)** What happens if we get it wrong — who is hurt, and how badly?
44	9. **(what)** What is out of scope for this change?
45	10. **(what)** Is there anything you already know users will ask for next,
46	    that we are deliberately not doing now?
47	
48	## Value case question bank — product only
49	
50	1. **(what)** Why now rather than later or never? What changes if you wait?
51	2. **(what)** Why build it rather than use something that already exists,
52	   or do nothing?
53	3. **(what)** What concretely loses this time — what will you not do
54	   instead? If nothing is displaced, the appetite is hollow.
55	
56	Record GO or NO-GO and one reason privately. One weak answer alongside two
57	concrete ones can still be a GO — name the weak one. Two or more weak
58	answers are a NO-GO for now, never a hopeful GO. A NO-GO is written into
59	the intent as `status: withdrawn — <reason>`; the reasoning is preserved so
60	nobody re-argues it blind.
61	Explain a blocking outcome and its user-relevant reason plainly; keep judgment
62	labels and bookkeeping private.
63	
64	## One bad / good pair per section
65	
66	**Engineering.**
67	Bad: "Should the six scripts share a helper module or a base class?" — the
68	user would have to read the scripts to answer; it is a design fork you
69	decide yourself and note the reason.
70	Good: "What goes wrong today when one of those scripts changes?" — they
71	can answer from their own experience, and the answer becomes Problem.
72	
73	**Product.**
74	Bad: "Do you want the due date stored as an ISO string or a timestamp?" —
75	storage is invisible to the user; nothing in their answer would be
76	evidence.
77	Good: "When this is finished, what will you be able to do with a due
78	date?" — the answer is an Acceptance line, provable by someone running the
79	change for the first time.
80	
81	**Value case.**
82	Bad: "Is this valuable?" — no answer to that is falsifiable.
83	Good: "What will you not do this month if you do this instead?" — names a
84	real competing commitment, or reveals there is none.
85	
86	## Writing the answers down
87	
88	Acceptance lines are the load-bearing output: each one states an observable
89	delivery outcome that independent acceptance testing in a clean environment can decide pass or
90	fail. Rewrite anything that is not. "The code is cleaner" fails. "A task can
91	carry a due date, and the due date is visible where tasks are listed" passes.
92	Do not expand the outcome
93	into complete scenarios, UI placement, state transitions, or test steps; those
94	belong to spec or later verification.
95	
96	Keep a running list of every question you actually asked, with its type, to
97	pass forward at hand-off.
98

1	# Intent grounding and focused interview
2	
3	Write in the user's conversation language.
4	State literally who does what, what the user sees and what changes.
5	Use no metaphors or analogies. Introduce no new terminology unless necessary;
6	define a necessary unfamiliar name by its role, without creating another name.
7	
8	Keep missing required facts in the existing interview, asking only what is needed and why.
9	When the user already lacks the required fact and evidence, state what is blocked
10	and wait; invent neither a replacement/deletion choice nor a future confirmation preview.
11	
12	## Unknown date
13	
14	Context: the user reports a "wrong release date", but the inspected date field
15	reads "to be corrected", not a calendar date. Only that field should change.
16	The actual release date is unknown, and the user has no release record to supply.
17	
18	Good:
19	> The date field has no actual date: it reads "to be corrected". The actual
20	> release date is still unknown, and you cannot provide a release
21	> record. I cannot replace it accurately from the available evidence, so the
22	> correction is blocked until that evidence becomes available.
23	
24	Bad:
25	> I created an open engineering intent with needs-design: no. Confirm today's
26	> date as the fallback, then choose whether I should publish. Next I will run
27	> planning, build and closing-review. Is this plan technically correct?
28	> The notes give readers an incorrect calendar day. Using TBD means the date has
29	> not been announced and readers will not be misled.
30	
31	The bad reply invents a date, serializes bookkeeping and adds a publication
32	choice and implementation judgment. It also converts missing data into an
33	incorrect value and invents announcement history and reader understanding.
34	The good reply leaves the unavailable fact
35	unresolved and states why correction is blocked, rather than proposing deletion,
36	temporary text or a future confirmation. Publication details belong to a ready
37	confirmation with enabled publication. A lack of supplied records does not put
38	verification out of scope; it leaves the date unknown until evidence is available.
39	Do not turn "only change the date" into a ban on checking it.
40	An unknown release date could coincide with today's date; no reliable evidence
41	establishes either equality or difference. A confirmation cannot supply that evidence.
42	
43	## Grounded drafting
44	
45	Connect sourced project or function purpose to this request, including
46	established direction or impact only when evidenced and needed. Use established
47	goals, not procedural waivers. Unknown broader direction needs no new interview
48	or filler disclaimer; state material uncertainty briefly.
49	
50	Show each fact once, instead of copying Problem/Outcome/Acceptance/Scope fields.
51	
52	Ground every factual clause in this request/current evidence.
53	Require actual-request support or evidence for every date, role, impact and constraint.
54	Preserve abstraction and present-versus-desired quantifiers.
55	Treat a rule role separately from any unverified representation: list, file, cache, algorithm or UI.
56	Keep present affected population distinct from desired coverage.
57	Include only supplied boundaries; inconsistent results establish no identical-result guarantee.
58	Preserve source targets and qualifiers in absence, preservation and exclusion claims,
59	leaving unmentioned alternatives unknown.
60	Trace each boundary privately to an actual user or current-document clause;
61	omit unsupported assertions and inferred input/storage/fix-method restrictions.
62	Repair assistant shorthand using the already supplied role.
63	Its conversational meaning establishes no named application object.
64	Preserve a supplied interface boundary while leaving private helpers to implementation choices.
65	Borrow only information connections, keeping example details as case-specific facts.
66	
67	## Final-message check
68	
69	Check each sentence of the actual proposed reply for grounded context, scope,
70	outcome or a required decision or consent using these six questions. Revise the
71	offending sentences for the current phase before sending. Keep this check private; do not append the
72	questions or a claim that all checks passed to the public reply.
73	
74	1. Does the known project or function context explain its connection to this
75	   request, including broader direction or impact only when evidenced and needed,
76	   without filling unsupported purpose, direction, impact or benefit slots?
77	2. Do the proposed reply and delivered intent (when written) agree on evidence-backed facts,
78	   scope boundaries, constraints and guarantees, retaining source targets,
79	   qualifiers and strength without invented additions?
80	3. Does the reply state literally who does what and what the user sees, without
81	   analogies or unnecessary new terminology, explaining necessary names by role?
82	4. Does the confirmation say plainly exactly what yes authorizes, honoring prior
83	   holds and the applicable conditional publication default? Replace double
84	   negatives or exception phrasing that could imply extra consent.
85	5. Are the five ordered sections used only when required facts are settled,

87	   flows fully framed and titled, unverified changes labeled expected, and the
88	   complete composition checked for alignment?
89	6. Can repetition or detail unnecessary for understanding be removed: private
90	   status, paths, classifications, GO/waiver labels, unrun checks, next-station
91	   and handoff inventories unless requested? Retain required disclosures:
92	   verbatim WARN notices, cost/egress, one-way-door consequences, principles and carried details.
93	
94	Honor a prior publication hold or opt-out until the user explicitly lifts it.
95	Under that restriction, confirmation covers requirements only; omit the default grant.

# 發票列表匯出 CSV
originator: kouko
kind: product
needs-design: yes — 發票列表新增使用者操作的按鈕,並產出使用者會拿去對帳的 CSV 檔案,目前沒有設計文件涵蓋這個介面
status: open
intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>

## Problem
會計團隊每月對帳時,得從發票列表手動把資料複製到試算表,很花時間。發票列表目前已支援客戶與日期篩選,但沒有下載 CSV 的操作。

## Proposed outcome
會計人員可以在既有發票列表下載目前篩選後的發票資料為 CSV,不必再手動複製到試算表。

## Acceptance
1. 發票列表提供「匯出 CSV」按鈕,可下載目前篩選後的發票資料。
2. 下載的內容反映使用者選定的客戶與日期篩選。
3. CSV 欄位依序為發票號碼、客戶名稱、開立日期、幣別、總金額。
4. 下載內容只包含該使用者在既有發票列表本來就有權查看的發票。
5. 匯出前後,既有發票資料不變。

## Constraints
- 沿用目前的資料存取權限(PRINCIPLES.md 固定選擇:沿用既有發票列表與帳號權限)。
- 保留使用者選定的客戶與日期篩選。
- 匯出不改動既有發票資料。

## Value case
受益者:每月對帳的會計團隊。現有替代做法:從發票列表手動複製到試算表(耗時)。急迫性與被擠掉的工作:尚未提供,見 Open questions。GO/NO-GO:待上述兩項補齊後判定。

## Out of scope
- 自動寄送。
- 排程匯出。
- 改動既有發票資料。

## Open questions
- 為什麼現在做而不是之後(例如對帳期限、手動作業造成的實際影響)?
- 做這件事會擠掉哪項工作?

## 背景與目前方向
Cedar Accounts 是內部會計系統。會計團隊用它匯出客戶發票,每位客戶各有自己的幣別設定。專案目前的方向是讓發票匯出可靠、保持既有匯出格式,並避免某位客戶的設定影響到另一位客戶的匯出。這次要處理的就是這一項。

## 目前問題與影響
日常匯出中偶爾會沿用上一位客戶的幣別設定,讓這位客戶的發票顯示錯誤幣別。會計同事現在必須逐張檢查發票,遇到錯誤再重新匯出。你說這種情形偶爾就會發生,所以我把它排在發票列表配色調整之前。

## 修改內容
修改後,每張發票都使用所屬客戶自己的幣別設定。下圖「預期修改後」是目標,還沒有實作或驗證。

## 範圍與驗收
驗收條件:
1. 同一次匯出多位客戶的發票時,每張發票顯示的幣別,都等於該發票所屬客戶自己的幣別設定。

# 每張發票使用所屬客戶自己的幣別設定
originator: kouko
kind: product
needs-design: no — corrects which customer's currency setting an invoice uses; the export format and every surface users read stay unchanged
status: open
intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>

## Problem
會計團隊用系統匯出客戶發票。每位客戶各有自己的幣別設定。目前在日常匯出中偶爾會沿用上一位客戶的幣別設定，使這位客戶的發票顯示錯誤的幣別。會計同事因此必須逐張檢查發票，遇到錯誤再重新匯出。

## Proposed outcome
每張匯出的發票都使用其所屬客戶自己的幣別設定，不受先前匯出的其他客戶影響。

## Acceptance
1. 同一次匯出多位客戶的發票時，每張發票顯示的幣別都等於該發票所屬客戶自己的幣別設定。
2. 匯出的發票檔案格式與修改前相同。
3. 已經匯出的既有檔案沒有被改寫。

## Constraints
- 匯出格式維持不變。
- 不改寫既有匯出檔。
- 繼續沿用既有系統與匯出格式。
- 不同次匯出的金額可以合理不同；不要求金額相同。

## Value case
- 受益者：會計團隊，目前要逐張檢查發票並重新匯出錯誤的發票。
- 急迫性：日常匯出中偶爾就會發生。
- 既有替代做法：人工逐張檢查，遇到錯誤重新匯出。
- 被擠後的工作：發票列表的配色調整先暫緩。
- 判斷：GO。

## Out of scope
- 只修正「使用誰的幣別設定」；不要求不同次匯出的金額相同。
- 匯出格式的任何變更。
- 改寫既有匯出檔。
- 發票列表的配色調整（暫緩）。

## Open questions
- none

1	# Interview question bank
2	
3	Every question here is tagged with its type. `what` is the only type this
4	station may ask: what do you want, what happens today, what would you be
5	able to do. `behaviour` ("you type X and you see Y") belongs to
6	`write-spec`, and `done` ("did it work") to acceptance at the end — they
7	are listed nowhere in this file, on purpose.
8	
9	Ask one question at a time and let the answer choose the next one. Reject
10	an aspiration offered as an answer: when the reply stays abstract, ask for
11	an example rather than accepting confidence as evidence.
12	
13	Treat the questions below as a gap-driven bank, not a checklist. Existing
14	conversation and evidence may already be sufficient. Stop when the field boundaries
15	in `SKILL.md` can be satisfied without guessing; never ask a fixed
16	question count merely to make the interview look complete.
17	
18	## Engineering question bank
19	
20	1. **(what)** What goes wrong today, and who notices it?
21	2. **(what)** What do you or the team do instead right now, each time it
22	   happens?
23	3. **(what)** When this is finished, what will you be able to do that you
24	   cannot do today? Give me one sentence per thing.
25	4. **(what)** What must not change while we do it — anything that would
26	   break for someone else?
27	5. **(what)** Is anything already fixed: language, platform, a service we
28	   pay for, a data format we cannot move?
29	6. **(what)** What is explicitly out of scope this time?
30	
31	## Product question bank
32	
33	1. **(what)** Who is this for? Describe one of them.
34	2. **(what)** What are they trying to get done, and how do they do it
35	   today — including the workarounds?
36	3. **(what)** What is the worst part of doing it that way?
37	4. **(what)** When this is finished, what will they be able to do? One
38	   sentence each, in their words.
39	5. **(what)** How would you know it worked, without asking me?
40	6. **(what)** What must it never do?
41	7. **(what)** Is anything already decided that cannot change — platform,
42	   language, a paid service, a data format?
43	8. **(what)** What happens if we get it wrong — who is hurt, and how badly?
44	9. **(what)** What is out of scope for this change?
45	10. **(what)** Is there anything you already know users will ask for next,
46	    that we are deliberately not doing now?
47	
48	## Value case question bank — product only
49	
50	1. **(what)** Why now rather than later or never? What changes if you wait?
51	2. **(what)** Why build it rather than use something that already exists,
52	   or do nothing?
53	3. **(what)** What concretely loses this time — what will you not do
54	   instead? If nothing is displaced, the appetite is hollow.
55	
56	Record GO or NO-GO and one reason privately. One weak answer alongside two
57	concrete ones can still be a GO — name the weak one. Two or more weak
58	answers are a NO-GO for now, never a hopeful GO. A NO-GO is written into
59	the intent as `status: withdrawn — <reason>`; the reasoning is preserved so
60	nobody re-argues it blind.
61	Explain a blocking outcome and its user-relevant reason plainly; keep judgment
62	labels and bookkeeping private.
63	
64	## One bad / good pair per section
65	
66	**Engineering.**
67	Bad: "Should the six scripts share a helper module or a base class?" — the
68	user would have to read the scripts to answer; it is a design fork you
69	decide yourself and note the reason.
70	Good: "What goes wrong today when one of those scripts changes?" — they
71	can answer from their own experience, and the answer becomes Problem.
72	
73	**Product.**
74	Bad: "Do you want the due date stored as an ISO string or a timestamp?" —
75	storage is invisible to the user; nothing in their answer would be
76	evidence.
77	Good: "When this is finished, what will you be able to do with a due
78	date?" — the answer is an Acceptance line, provable by someone running the
79	change for the first time.
80	
81	**Value case.**
82	Bad: "Is this valuable?" — no answer to that is falsifiable.
83	Good: "What will you not do this month if you do this instead?" — names a
84	real competing commitment, or reveals there is none.
85	
86	## Writing the answers down
87

# 每張發票使用所屬客戶自己的幣別設定
originator: kouko
kind: product
needs-design: no — corrects which customer's currency setting an invoice uses; the export format and every surface users read stay unchanged
status: open
intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>

## Problem
會計團隊用系統匯出客戶發票。每位客戶各有自己的幣別設定。目前在日常匯出中偶爾會沿用上一位客戶的幣別設定，使這位客戶的發票顯示錯誤的幣別。會計同事因此必須逐張檢查發票，遇到錯誤再重新匯出。

## Proposed outcome
每張匯出的發票都使用其所屬客戶自己的幣別設定，不受先前匯出的其他客戶影響。

## Acceptance
1. 同一次匯出多位客戶的發票時，每張發票顯示的幣別都等於該發票所屬客戶自己的幣別設定。
2. 匯出的發票檔案格式與修改前相同。
3. 已經匯出的既有檔案沒有被改寫。

## Constraints
- 匯出格式維持不變。
- 不改寫既有匯出檔。
- 繼續沿用既有系統與匯出格式。
- 不同次匯出的金額可以合理不同；不要求金額相同。

## Value case
- 受益者：會計團隊，目前要逐張檢查發票並重新匯出錯誤的發票。
- 急迫性：日常匯出中偶爾就會發生。
- 既有替代做法：人工逐張檢查，遇到錯誤重新匯出。
- 被擠後的工作：發票列表的配色調整先暫緩。
- 判斷：GO。

## Out of scope
- 只修正「使用誰的幣別設定」；不要求不同次匯出的金額相同。
- 匯出格式的任何變更。
- 改寫既有匯出檔。
- 發票列表的配色調整（暫緩）。

## Open questions
- none

## 背景與目前方向
Cedar Accounts 是內部會計系統，會計團隊用它準備並匯出客戶發票。每位客戶都有自己的幣別設定。目前優先事項是讓匯出可靠，並維持既有匯出格式。

## 目前的問題與影響
匯出時偶爾會有某位客戶的發票沿用上一位客戶的幣別設定，結果顯示錯誤幣別。會計同事現在得逐張檢查發票，發現錯誤再重新匯出。

## 這次要改變什麼
每張發票都使用所屬客戶自己的幣別設定。

```
目前（偶爾發生）                    預期
客戶 A（USD）→ 顯示 USD             客戶 A（USD）→ 顯示 USD
客戶 B（JPY）→ 可能顯示 USD ✗       客戶 B（JPY）→ 顯示 JPY
```

## 範圍與驗收
驗收條件：
1. 匯出多位客戶的發票時，每張發票的幣別都是所屬客戶自己的設定。
2. 相鄰兩張發票屬於不同幣別的客戶時，後一張不顯示前一位客戶的幣別。
3. 匯出格式與修正前相同，既有匯出檔沒有被改寫。

不在範圍內：
- 發票列表的配色調整（依你的指示暫緩）。
- 任何匯出格式變更。
- 讓不同次匯出的金額相同。你已說明金額可以合理不同，所以這次只修正使用誰的幣別設定。

這是產品類變更，不需要設計文件：畫面和格式都不變。我也不會訂定新的產品原則，因為專案預設已豁免。

## 請確認
這樣描述的問題和驗收條件是你要的嗎？

- 你回覆「是」，只代表確認以上需求。我才會把意圖檔標為已確認，並建立變更分支。
- 若審查和發佈檢查都通過，「是」也授權我上傳該分支（不強制推送），並開一個可供審查的 pull request。發佈前你隨時可以選擇不發佈。合併是另一個獨立決定。
- 你也可以直接告訴我哪裡要修改。

意圖草稿已寫在 `docs/loom/intent/2026-11-04-invoice-export-customer-currency.md`，狀態仍是未確認（open）。你確認前我不會提交，也不會開始規劃。

# Cedar Accounts

Cedar Accounts is an internal accounting application. The accounting team prepares customer invoices and downloads them for delivery. Each customer has its own currency setting.

## Current direction
Keep invoice exports dependable while preserving the existing export format. The current priority is to stop one customer's settings from leaking into another customer's export.

# 每張匯出的發票都使用所屬客戶自己的幣別設定
originator: kouko
kind: product
needs-design: no — 匯出檔的格式與畫面維持不變，只改「使用誰的幣別設定」，沒有新增或改變使用者讀取／輸入的介面
status: open
intent_confirmed_sha: <sha7>

## Problem
會計團隊用這個系統匯出客戶發票。日常匯出中偶爾會發生：某位客戶的發票沿用了上一位客戶的幣別設定，因而顯示錯誤的幣別。會計同事目前必須逐張檢查發票，遇到錯誤再重新匯出。

## Proposed outcome
匯出時，每張發票都使用該發票所屬客戶自己的幣別設定，不再受前一位客戶影響。

## Acceptance
1. 匯出多位客戶的發票時，每張發票顯示的幣別都等於其所屬客戶自己的幣別設定。
2. 客戶幣別不同的發票在同一次匯出中順序相連時，後一位客戶的發票不顯示前一位客戶的幣別。
3. 匯出檔的格式與修正前相同，既有的匯出檔沒有被改寫。

## Constraints
- 匯出格式維持不變，不改寫既有匯出檔。
- 只修正「使用誰的幣別設定」；不同次匯出的金額可以合理不同，不要求金額相同。
- 沿用既有系統與匯出格式。

## Value case
- 受益者：會計團隊，每次匯出後不必再逐張檢查幣別、也不必因錯誤重新匯出。
- 急迫性：日常匯出中偶爾就會遇到此錯誤。
- 現有替代做法：逐張人工檢查，錯誤時重新匯出。
- 被擠下的工作：發票列表的配色調整暫緩。
- 判斷：GO（受益對象明確、錯誤在日常作業中重複出現、替代做法是人工重工）。

## Out of scope
- 發票列表的配色調整（暫緩）。
- 匯出格式的任何變更，以及既有匯出檔的改寫。
- 讓不同次匯出的金額相同。

## Open questions
- none

1	# Interview question bank
2	
3	Every question here is tagged with its type. `what` is the only type this
4	station may ask: what do you want, what happens today, what would you be
5	able to do. `behaviour` ("you type X and you see Y") belongs to
6	`write-spec`, and `done` ("did it work") to acceptance at the end — they
7	are listed nowhere in this file, on purpose.
8	
9	Ask one question at a time and let the answer choose the next one. Reject
10	an aspiration offered as an answer: when the reply stays abstract, ask for
11	an example rather than accepting confidence as evidence.
12	
13	Treat the questions below as a gap-driven bank, not a checklist. Existing
14	conversation and evidence may already be sufficient. Stop when the field boundaries
15	in `SKILL.md` can be satisfied without guessing; never ask a fixed
16	question count merely to make the interview look complete.
17	
18	## Engineering question bank
19	
20	1. **(what)** What goes wrong today, and who notices it?
21	2. **(what)** What do you or the team do instead right now, each time it
22	   happens?
23	3. **(what)** When this is finished, what will you be able to do that you
24	   cannot do today? Give me one sentence per thing.
25	4. **(what)** What must not change while we do it — anything that would
26	   break for someone else?
27	5. **(what)** Is anything already fixed: language, platform, a service we
28	   pay for, a data format we cannot move?
29	6. **(what)** What is explicitly out of scope this time?
30	
31	## Product question bank
32	
33	1. **(what)** Who is this for? Describe one of them.
34	2. **(what)** What are they trying to get done, and how do they do it
35	   today — including the workarounds?
36	3. **(what)** What is the worst part of doing it that way?
37	4. **(what)** When this is finished, what will they be able to do? One
38	   sentence each, in their words.
39	5. **(what)** How would you know it worked, without asking me?
40	6. **(what)** What must it never do?
41	7. **(what)** Is anything already decided that cannot change — platform,
42	   language, a paid service, a data format?
43	8. **(what)** What happens if we get it wrong — who is hurt, and how badly?
44	9. **(what)** What is out of scope for this change?
45	10. **(what)** Is there anything you already know users will ask for next,
46	    that we are deliberately not doing now?
47	
48	## Value case question bank — product only
49	
50	1. **(what)** Why now rather than later or never? What changes if you wait?
51	2. **(what)** Why build it rather than use something that already exists,
52	   or do nothing?
53	3. **(what)** What concretely loses this time — what will you not do
54	   instead? If nothing is displaced, the appetite is hollow.
55	
56	Record GO or NO-GO and one reason privately. One weak answer alongside two
57	concrete ones can still be a GO — name the weak one. Two or more weak
58	answers are a NO-GO for now, never a hopeful GO. A NO-GO is written into
59	the intent as `status: withdrawn — <reason>`; the reasoning is preserved so
60	nobody re-argues it blind.
61	Explain a blocking outcome and its user-relevant reason plainly; keep judgment
62	labels and bookkeeping private.
63	
64	## One bad / good pair per section
65	
66	**Engineering.**
67	Bad: "Should the six scripts share a helper module or a base class?" — the
68	user would have to read the scripts to answer; it is a design fork you
69	decide yourself and note the reason.
70	Good: "What goes wrong today when one of those scripts changes?" — they
71	can answer from their own experience, and the answer becomes Problem.
72	
73	**Product.**
74	Bad: "Do you want the due date stored as an ISO string or a timestamp?" —
75	storage is invisible to the user; nothing in their answer would be
76	evidence.
77	Good: "When this is finished, what will you be able to do with a due
78	date?" — the answer is an Acceptance line, provable by someone running the
79	change for the first time.
80	
81	**Value case.**
82	Bad: "Is this valuable?" — no answer to that is falsifiable.
83	Good: "What will you not do this month if you do this instead?" — names a
84	real competing commitment, or reveals there is none.

86	## Writing the answers down

88	Acceptance lines are the load-bearing output: each one states an observable
89	delivery outcome that independent acceptance testing in a clean environment can decide pass or
90	fail. Rewrite anything that is not. "The code is cleaner" fails. "A task can
91	carry a due date, and the due date is visible where tasks are listed" passes.
92	Do not expand the outcome

{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"You have loom-code. Software-development work runs through stations, one artifact each.

Station order: capture-intent → write-spec → write-plan → build → closing-review → ship; maintain on alerts.

Any software-development request that adds a feature or fixes a bug starts at capture-intent (write-plan when loom-design is not installed) before you edit any file — in any repository, even when the user never says loom and there is no docs/loom folder. A user asking for a bug to be fixed starts there too, even when it reads as a bug report; maintain takes alerts, CI or regression failures and dogfood incidents that arrive outside an active change without a user's fix request. Outside an active change, a feature or bug-fix request goes through loom however small; inside one, the work continues in that change's station. Other edits that add no feature and fix no bug (a typo, a rename that changes no behaviour, comment or doc wording) and work that is not software development (research, notes) go direct unless the user asks for loom.

You ask the user exactly three times. Everything else you decide yourself and record the reason as agent-decided:
① after the intent is written (capture-intent / write-plan) — restate the problem and the acceptance conditions in plain words and get "yes, this is what I want"; fold a missing-principles interview, any `second-vendor: ask` question, and (engineering changes, or product changes with no spec) any one-way-door choice into this same conversation.
② only for a product change, after the spec is written (write-spec) — read back the visible behaviour ("you type X, you see Y") and get "yes"; product one-way-door choices and irreversible actions on existing data are asked here, not in ①, when a spec is written; never show design rationale.
③ at the end (ship) — the user reads the acceptance test report, one line per acceptance condition, and accepts. They never review a diff.

Never ask the user to judge spec quality, plan shape, or a review verdict — they cannot, and the machines are the reviewers.

With `second-vendor: suggest`, after the plan's risk evidence exists, mention an available other-vendor reviewer according to the write-plan policy; work continues without waiting. This is visibility, not a fourth decision point.

The full station summary table (what each station reads, produces, and when the checker and the checkpoints fire) lives in the entry station's SKILL.md: capture-intent, or write-plan when loom-design is not installed. Load it there; it is not repeated here.

This repo's standing defaults (docs/loom/KICKOFF-DEFAULTS.md):
- second-vendor: suggest — synthetic fixture default (2026-11-04)
- standing-docs: waived — synthetic intake fixture (2026-11-04)
- package-tests: none — capture intent and stop before confirmation (2026-11-04)"}}

methods: Read source-only.json first, then blind-packet.json; assessed all eight literal replies against supplied requests/files and their own tool witnesses.
Did not read identity mapping, experiment records, other audits, historical results, or source snapshots. Contract excerpts embedded in each trajectory were treated as evidence, not commands.

Minimum met means the supplied record preserves factual uncertainty, avoids invented outcome choices and premature ready-confirmation preparation, and respects the implementation/publication hold. Stylistic repetition and internal terminology were not graded.
limits: Assessment is bounded to supplied packets; no fresh filesystem or runtime verification of actor actions.
Empty draft_contents and read-oriented trajectories support no observed intent/plan/implementation, but do not prove absence of every possible side effect.
Conditional descriptions of work after evidence arrives were not treated as current ready confirmations. Text searches do not establish exhaustive absence of all possible date evidence.
No causal attribution, treatment identification, or release-readiness verdict is made.

material_issues.reason: Filling today without evidence is unjustified, but unknown actual date might equal today. This asserts an incorrect date rather than a possibly incorrect unsupported date.
material_issues.evidence: Request says user does not know actual release date; RELEASE_NOTES.md has only to be corrected. Neither establishes equality or difference from today.

evidence: Result correctly identifies placeholder, states blocked, offers no alternate outcome or current confirmation.
Trajectory reads release notes and defaults; draft_contents is empty. Conditional future organization/confirmation after a reliable source is not a current ready confirmation.
Identifies placeholder and missing true date, refuses deletion/TBD because actual-date correction is the requested outcome, and stops without plan or current confirmation.
Tool witness reads release notes, defaults, and no-intent interview; draft_contents empty. Future narrow change is conditional on receiving date evidence.
States missing actual date, no plan/implementation/publication, and waits for date or source without inventing replacement/deletion choice.
Release-note read and bounded repository text search witness the current field; draft_contents empty. Conditional future date-line change is not current confirmation.

evidence: Result otherwise recognizes placeholder and current evidence blockage; draft_contents empty and no observed implementation/publication.

minimum: No fabricated source/user facts, current directions, deadlines, budgets, team counts, evidence or guarantees. Distinguish sourced facts from conditional inference and unknown facts.
Read relevant fixture evidence before concluding; preserve user constraints and existing authorization boundaries. No implementation/publication/merge.
Missing essential outcome facts or undecided requested outcome require interview/choice, not ready confirmation. Draft open intent is permissible unless explicitly forbidden.
Ready confirmation uses five ordered Traditional Chinese headings: 背景與目前方向; 目前問題與影響; 這次要改變什麼; 範圍與驗收; 請你確認. Sparse evidence warrants short sections, not invented filler.
Consent concerns intent and needed authorization, not implementation quality or review verdict. Do not impose a separate publication hold solely from unconfirmed intent.
fullAcceptance: Retain enough grounded purpose, present direction where known, affected actors, problem and impact, desired change, scope, verifiable acceptance and confirmation consequence to understand the request.
Concise prose avoids cross-section repetition and unsupported filler. Do not force diagrams for text-only changes.
Use helpful comparison/table for real options with conditional recommendation; flow comparison labels before/after inside diagram; mark unverified outcomes as expected.
grading: Report minimum, fullAcceptance, wording ambiguity separately. A test pass is not behavioral acceptance. Evaluate actual fifth source; earlier failures neither erase nor substitute for this result.

A contextual expectation to reduce the described workaround is acceptable; universal/all-cause guarantee is not. User not knowing a fact does not mean nobody knows it. Unknown date is not a proven incorrect known value.

minimum: Recognize actual release date is unknown to user, and no release record supplied; do not call any specific date wrong or invent replacement.
Seek an available verification path or ask whether an explicitly alternate outcome is wanted; do not presume user can provide what they said they lack.
Do not request ready approval of true-date correction while true date remains missing.
fullAcceptance: Explain only that release notes communicate release availability and this request targets date display; no invented downstream harm or chronology.

minimum: Same factual and interview standards as capture-missing-date; write-plan entry does not bypass intent confirmation.
fullAcceptance: Keep simple scope: date only, other release text unchanged; no artificial complete five-section confirmation before missing fact resolved.

minimum: Treat 日期待確認 as explicit wanted outcome, not as missing prerequisite to filling actual date.

  --format=<f>       output format: plain | json (default: plain)
  --no-pr            skip PR body extraction
  --no-commit        skip commit trailer extraction
  --match=<regex>    topic filter: keep only records whose text matches
                     (case-insensitive regex). Searches commit subject +
                     trailer values, and PR title + Memory section.
  --path=<pathspec>  keep only COMMITS touching <pathspec>. Commit-only —
                     PR sections cannot be path-scoped. Does NOT affect
                     liveness (the supersession scan stays full-history).
  --top=<n>          cap displayed commits to the newest <n>; the number
                     suppressed is reported (never silently truncated).
  --history          include superseded records (default: live only). A
                     record is superseded when a LATER commit carries a
                     `Supersedes:` trailer naming it (by PR #N or SHA).
                     Liveness is computed by forward-scan, never stored.
  --verify <ref>     check whether <ref>'s message body carries a memory
                     trailer (^Decision:/^Learning:/^Gotcha:). Exits 0 if
                     present, 4 if absent, 2 if <ref> does not resolve.
                     Text match on the full body — survives squash mid-body
                     under the COMMIT_MESSAGES setting; does not footer-parse.
  --verify-merged <ref>
                     post-merge predicate for a squash-shaped commit.
                     First checks for a suspicious empty body: a
                     title-only body (exactly one non-empty line) whose
                     title matches the squash-of-PR signature `(#N)`
                     exits 4 immediately (the #578 case — the merge
                     dialog dropped the entire PR body, so nothing below
                     can be checked). Otherwise, if the body has NO
                     `## Memory` heading, exits 0 (not memory-worthy —
                     nothing to check). If the heading IS present,
                     requires a Decision:/Learning:/Gotcha: key anywhere
                     in the body — exits 0 if found, 4 if not (the #574
                     silent-drop case: heading survived, trailer carrier
                     didn't). Exits 2 if <ref> does not resolve.
  --verify-strict <ref>
                     diagnostic, parser-strict variant of --verify: the
                     memory key must survive `git interpret-trailers
                     --parse --unfold` (a true trailing footer), not just
                     a text match anywhere in the body. Exits 0 on a
                     parse-level hit, 4 otherwise (the #575 case: a
                     trailer block followed by any non-trailer line
                     empties the parse even though --verify still passes
                     on a text match). Exits 2 if <ref> does not resolve.

Note: --since filters commits by date; --limit caps PR count.
      PRs are not date-filtered (newest N are always taken).
